results.name: CARBONATO: a botnet built around an AI agent
results.description: ThreatDown researchers discovered CARBONATO, a Docker botnet that exploits exposed Docker daemons on port 2375. The operation was uncovered through an unauthenticated Docker registry exposed since May 2026, revealing two parallel activities: distribution of trojanized cryptocurrency wallet applications and a botnet infrastructure. The botnet leverages Hermes Agent, an MIT-licensed open-source AI framework, modified with a custom prompt directing it to execute commands via Telegram, maintain persistence, and harvest credentials. The campaign infrastructure spans multiple hosting providers including Linode, Hetzner, and Contabo, with activity documented from October 2024 through August 2026.

results.name: Konni Hackers Target Ukraine With Malicious LNK Files and VelvetCake PowerShell Malware
results.description: North Korea-linked threat actors are conducting Operation Conflict Compass, targeting individuals and organizations focused on Ukraine using spear-phishing emails with malicious ZIP attachments. These contain LNK files disguised as PDFs with themes related to Russia-Ukraine peace plans, Ukrainian research, and geopolitical issues. When executed, the shortcuts retrieve malicious files from GitHub, deploying VBScript to establish persistence via scheduled tasks and delivering VelvetCake, a lightweight PowerShell-based task runner. VelvetCake contacts command-and-control infrastructure to download and execute additional scripts that perform reconnaissance, collect system information, enumerate security software, and capture screenshots. The campaign also utilized trojanized Zoom installers and leveraged infrastructure in South Korea and Ukraine, with activity observed since early August 2026 targeting diplomatic entities, think tanks, and NGOs.

results.name: VeloCloud Orchestrator SQL Injection Vulnerability
results.description: VeloCloud Orchestrator (VCO) on-premises versions contain a critical SQL injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users with minimal privileges to escalate to superuser operator access. Any user with Enterprise Read Only role can exploit this flaw to access privileged internal functionality, potentially compromising the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the orchestrator and managed data. The vulnerability is actively exploited, with specific malicious IP addresses identified. Affected versions include VCO 5.2.x prior to 5.2.3.18, 6.1.x prior to 6.1.3.10, and 6.4.x prior to 6.4.2.12. Hosted and dedicated VCO instances were already patched. Immediate upgrade to fixed releases is recommended, along with restricting web interface access and monitoring for suspicious activity.

results.name: SEO Poisoning Campaign Delivers New Armorsteal Malware
results.description: In September 2026, an SEO poisoning campaign distributed Armorsteal malware through fake websites impersonating Chocolatey package manager and Microsoft Activation Scripts (MAS) tool. Victims searching for software installation commands were presented with malicious PowerShell scripts that deployed Python-based malware protected by Pyarmor. The malware consists of three main components: a remote access module that communicates with command-and-control servers and verifies RSA-2048 signatures on received tasks; a surveillance module that logs keystrokes, monitors clipboard activity, hijacks cryptocurrency wallet addresses, and captures screenshots; and an information stealer targeting browser data, Discord tokens, cryptocurrency wallets, seed phrases, passwords, and SSH keys. The campaign employed anti-analysis techniques including cloud provider detection and code obfuscation, with infrastructure changes observed throughout the monitoring period.

results.name: StealC Is Back, and This Time It's a RAT
results.description: Four months after Operation Endgame dismantled StealC in June, its seller returned in October with Stadia, a full-featured remote access trojan that incorporates StealC's code verbatim. Unlike its predecessor, Stadia offers comprehensive remote administration capabilities including hidden desktop control, live command shell, file explorer, process manager, and in-memory loader, with the original StealC stealer functioning as one of six modules. The operator targets former StealC customers by offering a free month on the top-tier subscription priced at $900 monthly. Analysis reveals the binary shares byte-for-byte code with StealC version 3.5, particularly the Chromium App-Bound Encryption helper. The agent communicates via plain HTTP to three hardcoded IP addresses, uses RC4 encryption with Base64 encoding, and establishes persistence through hidden scheduled tasks under C:\ProgramData\ with randomized directory names impersonating legitimate updaters. The transformation from simple infostealer to full RAT...

results.name: Beyond the Sandbox: Leveraging Android Intrusion Logs to Expose Advanced Threats
results.description: Advanced Android threats increasingly operate beyond the standard application sandbox, requiring multi-layered detection strategies that combine on-device behavioral analysis with OS-level telemetry. Android's Delegated Scope enables enterprises to grant security applications access to security and network logs on managed devices without full MDM authority. The new Intrusion Logging feature extends similar forensic visibility to BYOD users through Advanced Protection on supported devices running Android 16 or later. This privacy-preserving capability allows users to collect and share encrypted security, DNS, and connection logs for analysis. The technical analysis demonstrates how these logs expose the complete RatHat attack chain, including Wireless Debugging self-pairing, ADB shell command execution, daemon staging, and command-and-control communications, providing actionable indicators of compromise across process execution, privileged operations, and network activity.

results.name: 2026 Year End Phishing Lures
results.description: As organizations approach year-end and fiscal close periods, employees face increased administrative activity in finance, HR, and IT departments. This heightened legitimate communication creates ideal cover for phishing campaigns. Attackers exploit year-end business processes by impersonating compensation adjustments, Q4 financial documents, access reviews, invoice follow-ups, and benefits statements. Multiple campaigns have been observed targeting organizations across sectors including aviation, telecommunications, manufacturing, real estate, technology, and financial services, with concentration in the Middle East. Attackers leverage SharePoint, Docusign, and Microsoft 365 themes, employing credential harvesting pages disguised as document-sharing portals. Generic protected-message lures prove effective by requiring minimal customization while appearing legitimate during busy periods when employees expect increased document requests and administrative deadlines.

results.name: RemControl: AI Built the Overlays. Victims Lose their PINs
results.description: Group-IB researchers discovered RemControl, a previously undocumented Android banking trojan operating as Malware-as-a-Service since May 2026. The malware targets over 30 financial institutions across Western Europe, the Middle East, and Canada through fake TVTap IPTV download pages distributed via malvertising. RemControl abuses Android Accessibility Service to inject phishing overlays, stream device screens in real-time, log keystrokes, and provide full remote control. The investigation revealed that the criminal infrastructure was inadvertently built using AI assistance, with complete AI-generated responses found verbatim in production phishing pages. The C2 panel documentation describes credential theft as quiz completion, suggesting developers deceived AI assistants into building fraud infrastructure under false pretenses. The threat actor UNKK operates the campaigns, with possible links to the Medusa UNKN affiliate botnet based on overlapping infrastructure patterns and naming conventions.

results.name: Mind the (Patch) Gap, Part 2: Fake Websites Used to Deploy Chrome & Windows 0-Day Exploits
results.description: In early September 2026, Chinese threat actor UTA0565 exploited unpatched zero-day vulnerabilities in Google Chrome and Microsoft Windows through sophisticated phishing campaigns. The actor registered fake domains impersonating legitimate organizations including China Digital Times and the Center for American Progress, sending targeted phishing emails to Asian government entities. Victims were directed to spoofed websites hosting an exploit chain leveraging CVE-2026-85046, CVE-2026-87491, and CVE-2026-85880. The attacks delivered CLEANGULP, a previously undocumented malware family with backdoor capabilities including command execution, file operations, and beacon object file execution. The malware communicated with command-and-control infrastructure via encrypted HTTP traffic using custom encoding. Multiple Chinese APT groups demonstrated coordinated access to this exploit kit, suggesting widespread sharing within the Chinese cyber espionage community during the vulnerability window.

results.name: Disposable Domains, Durable Hosting
results.description: Over five months, four distinct malicious chains operated through the same bulletproof hosting provider, AS202412 registered to OMEGATECH LTD in Seychelles. All chains began with fake CAPTCHA pages (ClickFix technique) that instructed victims to paste commands into Windows Run dialogs. The campaigns used disposable domains with similar naming patterns, compromised legitimate websites, and varied infrastructure including cloud storage, blockchain-resolved C2 addresses, and trojanized installers. Despite different payloads and staging methods, every chain initiated contact through AS202412. The provider expanded from initial allocations to announcing twenty-four /24 prefixes during the observation period. Most browser contacts ended at the lure page without execution, but successful compromises deployed stealers and remote access tools with persistence mechanisms surviving system reboots.
